3. Mr. Mayank Joshi, learned counsel for respondent no.3/wife.
Accordingly, IA No.2/2024 stands disposed of.

5. This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is filed by the petitioner/accused for quashing the impugned summoning order dated 02.12.2022 passed by the IVth Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun in Criminal Case No.8505 of 2022, 'State of Uttarakhand Vs. Rajendra Singh',
for the offences under Sections 498A, 504, 506 of IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S.
Nehru Colony, Dehradun; Charge sheet dated 14.08.2022; F.I.R./Case Crime No.0484 of 2021 dated 08.12.2021 as well as the entire proceedings of the aforesaid criminal case.

sentences.text: 6. Counsel for the petitioner/husband would submit that the matter has been amicably settled and compromise has taken place on 11.06.2024 in the High Court Mediation Centre, Nainital between the petitioner/husband and respondent no.3/wife and they are identified by their respective counsel.
Report of the Mediator to this effect is also on record.

7. The settlement deed has been annexed, wherein it is stated that both the parties have 2024:UHC:8306 settled their matrimonial disputes and the petitioner/husband is ready to pay total lump sum of 20,00,000/-(Twenty Lakh Rupees) as permanent alimony, as full and final one time settlement of entire maintenance to respondent no.3/wife; that, the petitioner/husband will pay 10,00,000/- (Ten Lakh Rupees) through Bank Draft at the time of filing divorce petition under C482/2355/2023 on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72266196/
1 Section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act; that, at the time of the second motion of mutual divorce petition under Section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act at Dehradun, the petitioner will pay 10,00,000/- (Ten Lakh Rupees).
8.

Counsel for the parties would submit that after payment of full and final settlement of 20,00,000/- (Twenty Lakh Rupees) both the parties shall not have any claim on any property of each other and the respondent wife shall not be entitled to claim any further amount from her husband and his family members.
9. Accordingly, the C482 petition is disposed of in terms of settlement /agreement arrived at between the parties.
10. Both the parties are bound by the consensual condition stated in the settlement/agreement filed in this petition.
